title: A Survey of Agent Memory in the Second Half: Towards Self-Evolving and Long-Horizon Agents
supports: 2026 survey of agent memory; organises the field along memory substrate / cognitive mechanism / memory subject and reviews evaluation benchmarks and metrics - the closest prior taxonomy to ours (type-level, not operation-level).

title: Are We Ready For An Agent-Native Memory System?
supports: States that agent memory is now a data management system (storage, retrieval, update, consolidation, lifecycle governance) while existing evaluations still report end-to-end task success with the system as a black box; proposes a four-module analytical framework and evaluates 12 systems. Primary motivation for our operation-level protocol.

title: Externalization in LLM Agents: A Unified Review of Memory, Skills, Protocols and Harness Engineering
supports: Reviews agent infrastructure as externalisation of state (memory), expertise (skills) and interaction (protocols); lists open challenges in evaluation and governance of external memory.

title: A Survey on the Memory Mechanism of Large Language Model based Agents
supports: Survey of the memory mechanism of LLM-based agents (memory sources, forms, operations); the operation vocabulary we extend with revision, prospective and epistemic-status operations.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
supports: RAG survey; three-paradigm decomposition (naive / advanced / modular) and the retrieval-generation-augmentation loop that agent memory retrieval inherits.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for AI-Generated Content: A Survey
supports: Second RAG survey covering retrieval granularity, training and evaluation axes; shows how heterogeneous retrieval metrics are reported, a comparability problem the protocol addresses.

title: Knowledge Conflicts for LLMs: A Survey
supports: Taxonomy of knowledge conflicts (context-memory, inter-context, intra-memory) for LLMs; the conflict classes our contradiction tasks instantiate.

title: Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models: A Survey
supports: Survey of knowledge editing (locate-then-edit, meta-learning, memory-based); the parametric counterpart to external belief revision.

title: What Twelve LLM Agent Benchmark Papers Disclose About Themselves: A Pilot Audit and an Open Scoring Schema
supports: Audit of twelve agent benchmark papers: two papers reporting on the same benchmark and model disagree and the paper text does not say why (scaffold, prompts, budget). Motivates the mandatory reporting block in our protocol.

title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
supports: MemGPT: virtual context management with main/external storage and OS-inspired paging - the archetype of the storage-tier model that our write/read operations must be expressed in.

title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
supports: Generative agents: memory stream with recency/importance/relevance retrieval and reflection over observations - canonical read-side scoring and offline consolidation.

title: MemoryBank: Enhancing Large Language Models with Long-Term Memory
supports: MemoryBank: long-term memory with Ebbinghaus-style decay and user-portrait summarisation - canonical forgetting/summarisation policy.

title: SCM: Enhancing Large Language Model with Self-Controlled Memory Framework
supports: Self-Controlled Memory: memory controller plus memory stream for long inputs - explicit control operations over the store.

title: RET-LLM: Towards a General Read-Write Memory for Large Language Models
supports: RET-LLM: a general read-write memory unit for LLMs with explicit write/read operations - the closest prior interface-level framing.

title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
supports: A-MEM: agentic memory with note construction, link generation and memory evolution - a write operation that mutates existing records.

title: Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
supports: Mem0: production memory layer that extracts, consolidates and retrieves salient facts, with a graph variant; reports accuracy/cost/latency against a full-context baseline.

title: MemOS: A Memory OS for AI System
supports: MemOS: memory as first-class resource with scheduling/management, incl. plaintext, activation and parameter memory - sharing across memory types.

title: Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory
supports: Zep/Graphiti: temporal knowledge graph memory with bi-temporal validity intervals; reports latency improvements and DMR accuracy against MemGPT.

title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
supports: HippoRAG: hippocampal-index inspired retrieval over a knowledge graph, single-step multi-hop retrieval - shows retrieval-architecture effects on memory QA.

title: On the Structural Memory of LLM Agents
supports: Comparative study of memory structures and retrieval methods for agent memory, including non-parametric structures; evidence that structure choice changes task outcomes.

title: Towards Effective GenAI Multi-Agent Collaboration: Design and Evaluation for Enterprise Applications
supports: Design and evaluation study of GenAI multi-agent collaboration for enterprise applications: reports design dimensions and evaluation practice for agent ensembles, the setting in which shared memory lives.

title: Collaborative Memory: Multi-User Memory Sharing in LLM Agents with Dynamic Access Control
supports: Collaborative memory across users with dynamic access control - memory as a shared resource with scoping, which our taxonomy treats as record metadata.

title: Memory as a Service (MaaS): Purpose-Bound Memory Mediation for Cooperative Agents
supports: Memory as a service: purpose-bound mediation of memories produced by many agents - motivates operation-level contracts between producer and consumer.

title: Oracle Agent Memory as an Enterprise Memory Substrate for Long-Horizon AI Agents
supports: Enterprise memory substrate for long-horizon agents; names the same requirements we treat as operations: retention of task state, cross-session facts, procedural knowledge, scoping and durability.

title: Hierarchical Long-Term Semantic Memory for LinkedIn's Hiring Agent
supports: Industrial hierarchical semantic memory (LinkedIn hiring agent); reports latency and extraction-quality constraints of a deployed store - cost/latency metrics are first-class, as in our protocol.

title: E-mem: Multi-agent based Episodic Context Reconstruction for LLM Agent Memory
supports: E-mem: argues that compressing episodic context into embeddings/graphs destroys dependencies (de-contextualisation); an anti-consolidation position our protocol can test rather than assume.

title: CraniMem: Cranial Inspired Gated and Bounded Memory for Agentic Systems
supports: CraniMem: gated, bounded memory with consolidation and distractor resistance; criticises ad-hoc read/write rules of database-like memory systems.

title: BaRe-Mem: Bayesian Reliability Memory for Robust and Adaptive Agent Consultation
supports: BaRe-Mem: online Bayesian reliability estimates per advisor - per-record reliability as a stored, updated quantity.

title: D-MEM: Dopamine-Gated Agentic Memory via Reward Prediction Error Routing
supports: D-MEM: reports O(N^2) write latency and token cost for append-and-evolve designs (A-MEM) and routes writes by reward prediction error; direct evidence that write cost must be measured, not assumed.

title: Did You Check the Right Pocket? Cost-Sensitive Store Routing for Memory-Augmented Agents
supports: Store routing: retrieval as a routing problem evaluated with coverage, exact match and token efficiency - shows token-efficiency metrics can be computed automatically.

title: Distilling Feedback into Memory-as-a-Tool
supports: Distils transient critiques into retrievable guidelines through a file-based memory and agent-controlled tool calls - an operation-level (write-what) ablation.

title: Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time
supports: Sleep-time compute: offline pre-computation over a context before queries arrive reduces inference cost - the offline consolidation operation and its cost model.

title: Knowing the Store: What a Memory Backend Must Write Down Before an Agent Can Read It
supports: Knowing the Store: a memory backend must expose value-free lifecycle metadata so an agent can tell that a record (cancelled plan) must not be used; scores that judgment as metamemory monitoring. Supports our metadata and inadmissible-record tasks.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
supports: RAG: retrieval-augmented generation over a non-parametric index; the baseline read path of every memory system we benchmark.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
supports: Self-RAG: self-reflective retrieval with critique tokens - retrieval decisions are themselves an operation with measurable outcomes.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
supports: Lost in the middle: retrieval/answer accuracy depends strongly on where evidence sits in the context - a confound our protocol fixes by masking evidence order.

title: Found in the Middle: Calibrating Positional Attention Bias Improves Long Context Utilization
supports: Found in the middle: positional attention bias can be calibrated to improve long context use - follow-up evidence for positional effects.

title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
supports: GraphRAG: query-focused summarisation over a derived entity graph; the graph-based consolidation path.

title: Agent Workflow Memory
supports: Agent workflow memory: inducing reusable workflows from past trajectories - procedural memory as an explicitly induced artefact.

title: Highlight-Then-Summarize: Learning to Compress Evidence for Long-Context Understanding
supports: Highlight-then-summarise compression of long context - a concrete compression policy whose fidelity loss the protocol measures.

title: ContextPipe: Database-Inspired Context Assembly for Long-Horizon Agents
supports: ContextPipe: context assembly under a hard token budget with ordering and compaction decisions - formalises the budget constraint our cost metrics share.

title: ConflictBank: A Benchmark for Evaluating the Influence of Knowledge Conflicts in LLM
supports: ConflictBank: benchmark for the influence of knowledge conflicts on LLMs; provides conflict constructions reusable in our contradiction-injection tasks.

title: Does RAG Know When Retrieval Is Wrong? Diagnosing Context Compliance under Knowledge Conflict
supports: Shows that final-answer accuracy hides whether a model followed retrieved evidence, its parametric prior or produced something else; our conflict tasks score the attribution decision separately from the answer.

title: Whose Facts Win? LLM Source Preferences under Knowledge Conflicts
supports: Source identity changes how LLM pipelines resolve conflicts - a variable our protocol controls for in conflict tasks.

title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT
supports: ROME: causal tracing locates factual associations that can be edited directly - the parametric alternative to writing a record.

title: Mass-Editing Memory in a Transformer
supports: MEMIT: mass editing of many facts at once; scales the rewrite operation and shows the cost of bulk revision.

title: A General Katsuno-Mendelzon-Style Characterization of AGM Belief Base Revision for Arbitrary Monotonic Logics
supports: Katsuno-Mendelzon-style characterisation of AGM belief base revision - the formal revision semantics our belief-revision operations are named after.

title: Towards a General-Purpose Belief Maintenance System
supports: Argues for a general-purpose belief maintenance system bridging probabilistic uncertainty and symbolic belief structures; the maintenance-component lineage.

title: Enriching a Model's Notion of Belief using a Persistent Memory
supports: Persistent memory of (subject, relation, object) belief statements makes a model's answers consistent - evidence that an external belief store changes internal consistency.

title: PROV-AGENT: Unified Provenance for Tracking AI Agent Interactions in Agentic Workflows
supports: PROV-AGENT: unified provenance for agent interactions, so reasoning can be inspected and errors traced - the model for our per-record provenance requirement.

title: Securing LLM-Agent Long-Term Memory Against Poisoning: Non-Malleable, Origin-Bound Authority with Machine-Checked Guarantees
supports: Non-malleable, origin-bound write authority with machine-checked guarantees against memory poisoning; supports treating write authority as part of the record.

title: Memory Poisoning Attack and Defense on Memory Based LLM-Agents
supports: Memory poisoning attack and defence on memory-based LLM agents; quantifies corruption of long-term memory via query-only interactions.

title: MRMMIA: Membership Inference Attacks on Memory in Chat Agents
supports: Membership inference against chat-agent memory - privacy leakage that a memory store's report must be able to bound.

title: Teaching Models to Express Their Uncertainty in Words
supports: Models can be trained to state confidence in words (e.g. '90% confidence') that is better calibrated than the corresponding probabilities - verbalised confidence is measurable without logit access.

title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
supports: Larger models are well calibrated on multiple-choice/true-false self-evaluation and can predict which questions they will answer correctly (P(IK)).

title: Just Ask for Calibration: Strategies for Eliciting Calibrated Confidence Scores from Language Models Fine-Tuned with Human Feedback
supports: Elicitation strategy, not just model scale, drives calibration quality of expressed confidence.

title: Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? An Empirical Evaluation of Confidence Elicitation in LLMs
supports: Black-box evaluation of confidence elicitation: no prompt strategy gives both good calibration and good discrimination; framework for measuring both.

title: Can AI Assistants Know What They Don't Know?
supports: Refusal-aware calibration of assistants: a model should decline outside its knowledge boundary; an operation-level abstention metric.

title: Are Large Language Models More Honest in Their Probabilistic or Verbalized Confidence?
supports: Compares probabilistic vs verbalised confidence: probabilistic confidence discriminates knowledge boundaries better while verbalised confidence is better calibrated in some regimes - hence we require both to be reported.

title: On Verbalized Confidence Scores for LLMs
supports: Verbalised confidence scores need explicit evaluation protocol and are prompt-sensitive - supports fixing elicitation prompts in our protocol.

title: Uncertainty Decomposition for Clarification Seeking in LLM Agents
supports: Decomposes uncertainty for clarification seeking in agents (underspecification-aware) - a third operation alongside asserting and abstaining.

title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
supports: Establishes reliability diagrams, ECE and temperature scaling for neural networks; the metric machinery we reuse for stored-confidence calibration.

title: Calibration of probabilities: The state of the art to 1980
supports: Human probability calibration review (overconfidence, calibration vs resolution); the origin of the reliability-diagram framing for stored confidence.

title: PM-Bench: Evaluating Prospective Memory in LLM Agents
supports: PM-Bench: text-based benchmark measuring prospective memory (executing an intention at a future cue while other activity continues) - the single operation our prospective-memory tasks must reuse rather than reinvent.

title: Making Prospective Memory SLM-Shaped: Typed Intention Stores for Small-Model Agents
supports: Typed intention stores for small-model agents: reports that the best published PM-Bench scaffold reaches limited accuracy - baseline numbers for PM tasks.

title: Normal aging and prospective memory.
venue: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition, 1990
supports: Experimental evidence that prospective memory (intention for a future cue) is a distinct faculty that ages differently from retrospective recall - the psychological basis for treating it as its own operation.

title: The Soar Cognitive Architecture
supports: The Soar cognitive architecture: separate declarative (semantic/episodic) and procedural memories with a working-memory graph - the canonical multi-store design our taxonomy maps onto MCP servers.

title: An Analysis and Comparison of ACT-R and Soar
supports: Detailed comparison of ACT-R and Soar representations, metadata and processing - evidence that the field's store boundaries differ per architecture, hence the need for an operation-level (not structure-level) taxonomy.

title: An Integrated Theory of the Mind.
supports: ACT-R: integrated theory of mind with declarative/procedural distinction and activation-based retrieval - activation and retrieval-probability metrics.

title: Hybrid Personalization Using Declarative and Procedural Memory Modules of the Cognitive Architecture ACT-R
supports: Hybrid personalisation with ACT-R declarative and procedural memory modules - separates what is stored from how it is used, as our taxonomy does.

title: Analogical Concept Memory for Architectures Implementing the Common Model of Cognition
supports: Analogical concept memory for Common-Model-of-Cognition architectures: generalisation across episodes is a memory operation, not a retrieval side effect.

title: Human Memory: A Proposed System and its Control Processes
supports: The multi-store model (sensory, short-term, long-term with control processes) - control processes are the ancestors of our write/consolidate operations.

title: The magical number seven, plus or minus two: Some limits on our capacity for processing information.
supports: Capacity limits on immediate memory - the quantitative ancestor of a context/token budget.

title: Levels of processing: A framework for memory research
venue: Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior, 1972
supports: Depth of processing determines later recall: what you store at write time predicts read success - the write-side quality metric.

title: Encoding specificity and retrieval processes in episodic memory.
supports: Encoding specificity: retrieval depends on the match between encoding context and retrieval cue - the theoretical basis for probe-set/provenance requirements.

title: Source monitoring.
supports: Source monitoring: remembering where knowledge came from is a distinct process that fails independently of content recall - the human evidence for provenance as a separate scoring dimension.

title: Spacing Effects in Learning
supports: Spacing effects in learning: gap between exposures changes retention - informs the schedule of consolidation runs.

title: The Power of Testing Memory: Basic Research and Implications for Educational Practice
supports: Retrieval practice improves long-term retention more than restudy - evidence that read operations themselves modify the store's future usefulness.

title: Sleep-Dependent Learning and Memory Consolidation
supports: Sleep-dependent memory consolidation: offline replay is a necessary post-encoding process - the biological analogue of the offline consolidation operation.

title: A Robotic Model of Hippocampal Reverse Replay for Reinforcement Learning
supports: Computational model of hippocampal reverse replay for reinforcement learning - a mechanism-level account of offline consolidation.

title: Human-like Forgetting Curves in Deep Neural Networks
supports: Tests whether artificial models show human-like Ebbinghaus forgetting curves under decay and spaced repetition - measurable decay shaping.

title: FOREVER: Forgetting Curve-Inspired Memory Replay for Language Model Continual Learning
supports: Forgetting-curve-inspired replay scheduling for continual learning - an explicit retention-policy benchmark.

title: Simulating Human Memory with Language Models
supports: Runs classic human memory experiments on language models and reports that LM memory is far more reliable than human memory - warning against anthropomorphic decay assumptions.

title: Evaluating Long-Term Memory in 3D Mazes
supports: Long-term memory evaluation in partially observed 3D mazes (Memory Maze) - an environment-level memory benchmark with leakage controls.

title: Specification - Model Context Protocol
supports: Model Context Protocol specification revision 2025-06-18: server/client discovery, tools, resources and prompts - the interface our protocol binds to.

title: Specification - Model Context Protocol
supports: Earlier MCP revision (2025-03-26) - kept to show which revision a reported run targeted.

title: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)? - Model Context Protocol
supports: MCP introduction: the protocol's stated purpose of standardising how applications give LLMs context and tools.

title: Introducing the Model Context Protocol \ Anthropic
supports: MCP announcement (November 2024) - the primary source for the protocol's origin and stated goals.

title: GitHub - modelcontextprotocol/servers: Model Context Protocol Servers · GitHub
supports: Reference MCP server collection - the harness that makes the protocol concrete and the population our protocol must work against.

title: JSON-RPC 2.0 Specification
supports: JSON-RPC 2.0 specification: request/response/error framing used by MCP transports - the source of our error-code accounting.

title: MCP-Universe: Benchmarking Large Language Models with Real-World Model Context Protocol Servers
supports: MCP-Universe: benchmark for LLMs driving real MCP servers across 6 domains, 231 tasks; shows the ecosystem is benchmarkable at task level.

title: MCPToolBench++: A Large Scale AI Agent Model Context Protocol MCP Tool Use Benchmark
supports: MCPToolBench++: large-scale MCP tool-use benchmark with cost analysis - precedent for reporting per-call cost in MCP evaluations.

title: Evaluation Report on MCP Servers
supports: MCPBench: an evaluation framework for MCP servers measuring task effectiveness and efficiency (latency, tokens) - the closest prior art to a runnable, implementation-agnostic MCP evaluation, but scoped to tool-use tasks, not to memory operations.

title: MCP-SafetyBench: A Benchmark for Safety Evaluation of Large Language Models with Real-World MCP Servers
supports: MCP-SafetyBench: safety evaluation of LLMs with real MCP servers - evidence that protocol-level benchmarking of servers is an accepted practice.

title: MCP Server Architecture Patterns for LLM-Integrated Applications
supports: MCP server architecture patterns and ecosystem growth after November 2024 - context for why a memory-server protocol is actionable now.

title: What a Random Draw from the MCP Registry Contains, and What Tool-Use Benchmarks Contain Instead
supports: Shows that MCP ecosystem studies select for servers that work (reference sets, popularity, repaired pipelines) - warns that our server sample must be reported explicitly.

title: Unicode TAG-Block Concealment of Tool-Metadata Payloads in the Model Context Protocol: An Approval-View Fidelity Gap Across Three Independent Server Implementations
supports: Unicode TAG-block concealment of tool metadata across three MCP server implementations: an approval-view fidelity gap - a class of metadata-integrity checks our protocol's provenance task must include.

title: Retrieval Models Aren't Tool-Savvy: Benchmarking Tool Retrieval for Large Language Models
supports: Tool retrieval benchmarks: as tool sets grow, retrieving the right tool becomes the bottleneck - the same finding our memory-store routing task tests for records.

title: citecheck: An MCP Server for Automated Bibliographic Verification and Repair in Scholarly Manuscripts
supports: citecheck: an MCP server that verifies and repairs bibliographic metadata - evidence that protocol servers can carry machine-checkable verification procedures.

title: AI Agents with Decentralized Identifiers and Verifiable Credentials
supports: Agent identity with decentralised identifiers and verifiable credentials for agent-to-agent trust - the credentialing direction our origin-bound write authority points to.

title: Agent Network Protocol Technical White Paper
supports: Agent Network Protocol white paper: interoperability requirements between heterogeneous agents (identity, discovery, negotiation).

title: AWCP: A Workspace Delegation Protocol for Deep-Engagement Collaboration across Remote Agents
supports: AWCP: workspace delegation protocol between remote agents - shows protocol work in agent ecosystems is moving to explicit, testable interfaces.

title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
supports: LongMemEval: 500 questions over five long-term-memory abilities (information extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, knowledge updates, abstention) - the ability list our task families must align with or extend.

title: Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents
supports: LoCoMo: very long-term multi-session dialogue benchmark with QA and event-graph summarisation; reports that long-context and RAG models lag humans - baseline reference.

title: DialSim: A Dialogue Simulator for Evaluating Long-Term Multi-Party Dialogue Understanding of Conversational Agents
supports: DialSim: simulator for long-term multi-party dialogue understanding with time constraints - shows how timing constraints enter memory evaluation.

title: SGMem: Sentence Graph Memory for Long-Term Conversational Agents
supports: SGMem: sentence-graph memory that keeps provenance instead of reducing context to isolated facts; reports gains on long-conversation tasks.

title: Beyond Static Dialogues: Benchmarking Realistic, Heterogeneous, and Evolving Long-Term Memory
supports: Benchmark with evolving personas and long-horizon semantic consistency across sessions - criteria the protocol's multi-session tasks adopt.

title: IFCMemoryBench: Evaluating Long-Term Memory of LLM-Based Agents in BIM Information Retrieval
supports: IFCMemoryBench: domain memory benchmark (BIM) arguing that non-domain, persona-grounded evaluations are weaker tests - supports domain-transfer tasks.

title: AEMA: Verifiable Evaluation Framework for Trustworthy and Controlled Agentic LLM Systems
supports: AEMA: verifiable evaluation framework for agentic LLM systems with coordination and decision transparency metrics - precedent for verifiable report artefacts.

title: TWIST: A Proposed Benchmark for Intervention Quality in Conversational Memory, with a Human-Validated Draft-Alignment
supports: TWIST: proposes measuring the quality of memory interventions (not only recall), with a human-validated alignment - adjacent to our revision-quality scoring.

title: The Right Memory in the Wrong Context: Verifying Retrieval Admissibility in Long-Term Agent Memory
supports: Verifies retrieval admissibility (principal, policy, lifecycle state) in long-term agent memory: shows that recall and answer accuracy cannot detect inadmissible retrieval - a single-operation protocol we must cite and extend, not duplicate.

title: When Retrieval Fails Before It Begins: Structurally Indirect Prerequisite Eviction as a Retention Failure in Agentic Memory
supports: Isolates a pre-retrieval retention failure mode (structurally indirect prerequisite eviction) - evidence that retention must be scored separately from retrieval.

title: Power Systems Agent Benchmark: Executable Evaluation of AI Agents in Electric Power Engineering
supports: Power Systems Agent Benchmark: executable evaluation of agents in electric power engineering - precedent for checking consequences with a program rather than grading prose, in the industrial domain this work is intended to transfer to.

title: Large Language Model Evaluation Via Multi AI Agents: Preliminary results
supports: Multi-agent LLM evaluation attempt with reported inconsistencies between graders - reason to prefer programmatic checks where possible.

title: HARMONY: A Scalable Distributed Vector Database for High-Throughput Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
supports: HARMONY: distributed vector database for high-throughput ANNS - the retrieval backend whose throughput ceiling bounds read cost.

title: Approximate Diverse $k$-nearest Neighbor Search in Vector Database
supports: Approximate diverse k-NN search in vector databases; diversity as a first-class retrieval objective - the metric our retrieval-diversity measurement borrows.

title: Organization and maintenance of large ordered indexes
supports: B-tree organisation and maintenance - the index-maintenance cost model behind write latency.

title: Database File Format
supports: SQLite database file format - a durable single-file store whose documented format lets an evaluation snapshot and re-open a memory store byte-for-byte.

title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication
supports: Shannon's measure of information: bits as the unit in which we report raw context and record payload sizes.

title: A New Approach to Linear Filtering and Prediction Problems
supports: Recursive state estimation with uncertainty - the classical form of the belief-plus-uncertainty update that calibrated confidence generalises.

supports: PROV-O: the W3C provenance ontology (entity/activity/agent, wasDerivedFrom, wasGeneratedBy, wasInvalidatedBy) - the standard vocabulary our record provenance block reuses instead of inventing one.

supports: A vendor memory tool exposed to agents with explicit operations over a file-based store - evidence that production agents already expose memory as an interface.

supports: Vendor guidance on managing finite context (compaction, structured note-taking, sub-agents) - the practical motivation for external memory operations.

supports: Mem0 documentation: managed memory layer with add/search/update operations - a hosted memory API whose operations map onto our taxonomy.
